newsitem.title: INDIA: India planters told to plant more rubber.
newsitem.headline: India planters told to plant more rubber.

text.p: Indian growers were urged on Monday to plant rubber in non traditional areas in northern and eastern states.

The chairman of the state-run Rubber Board, K.J. Mathew, told a conference organised by the United Planters' Association of Southern India that it was incorrect to say that plantations in non traditional areas would be unviable.
"Don't forget that even in traditional areas, about 40 percent of the growers obtain a productivity level lower than the economically viable and optimum level," Mathew said.
He said that new plantations in non-traditional areas involved greater efforts like efficiency, training of manpower and financial commitments.
These were not only possible but essential, he said.
Mathew said that while India had come a long way in natural rubber production, it was far from self-sufficiency.
Indian plantations in 1996-97 (April-March) are likely to produce a record 547,000 tonnes of rubber from an area of 525,000 hectares.
"Still, there is a gap (between domestic production and domestic consumption) of 31,000 tonnes which would widen to 60,000 tonnes in the year 2000 and 300,000 tonnes in the year 2011," he said.
To make India self-sufficient, it is necessary to produce 1.2 million tonnes by the year 2011, for which an additional area of 36,000 hectares would have to be brought under rubber.
"This explains the need to go for non-traditional areas, since the land availability is limited in the traditional belts," he said.
Mathew said there was also the need to raise productivity from the present 1,420 kgs per hectare to 1,800 kgs by the year 2011 along with the planned increase in the area.
